chain.label: Flight crew fatigue from transmeridian schedule and circadian trough timing
chain.trigger: the flight crew was experiencing fatigue, which likely degraded their performance during the approach

chain.label: PF's 777 transition training did not include straight-in, speed-restricted visual approaches without an ILS glideslope
chain.trigger: the PF's inadequate training on the planning and execution of visual approaches

chain.label: Boeing documentation and Asiana training inadequately described 777 A/T HOLD-mode and automatic-engagement logic
chain.trigger: the complexities of the autothrottle and autopilot flight director systems that were inadequately described in Boeing's documentation and Asiana's pilot training, which increased the likelihood of mode error

chain.label: Flight crew mismanaged the airplane's descent after accepting the 180-knot ATC speed restriction, leaving it well above the desired glidepath at 5 nm
chain.trigger: the flight crew mismanaged the airplane's descent, which resulted in the airplane being well above the desired 3° glidepath when it reached the 5 nm point

caused_by.evidence: the PF's inadequate training on the planning and execution of visual approaches

chain.label: PF selected FLCH SPD pitch mode, with the MCP altitude set above the airplane's current altitude, to increase descent rate
chain.trigger: the pilot flying (PF) selected an autopilot (A/P) mode (flight level change speed [FLCH SPD]) that instead resulted in the autoflight system initiating a climb

caused_by.evidence: In an attempt to increase the airplane's descent rate and capture the desired glidepath, the pilot flying (PF) selected...FLCH SPD
the PF had an inaccurate understanding of how the Boeing 777 A/P and A/T systems interact to control airspeed in FLCH SPD mode

chain.label: Autoflight system responded to the FLCH SPD selection by beginning an unwanted climb toward the MCP altitude
chain.trigger: the AFCS responded to the mode change by starting to slow the airplane...and initiating a climb toward the MCP-selected target altitude of 3,000 ft

caused_by.evidence: AFDS pitch mode changed to FLCH SPD, and the A/T mode changed to thrust (THR) mode

chain.label: PF disconnected the autopilot and manually retarded the thrust levers to idle to counter the climb
chain.trigger: The PF disconnected the A/P and moved the thrust levers to idle

caused_by.evidence: the AFCS-initiated forward movement of the thrust levers...was manually overridden, and the thrust levers were moved aft

chain.label: Autothrottle transitioned to HOLD mode, deactivating automatic airspeed control
chain.trigger: which caused the A/T to change to the HOLD mode, a mode in which the A/T does not control airspeed

caused_by.evidence: the thrust levers reached the idle position, and the A/T mode changed to HOLD

chain.label: PM turned off only the PF's flight director switch, not his own, so the FLCH SPD/HOLD condition was never cleared
chain.trigger: the two F/D switches were not both in the off position at the same time. If they had been, the A/T mode would have changed to speed mode and maintained the approach speed

caused_by.evidence: the AFDS remained active and continued to display the FLCH SPD guidance that the PF had commanded

chain.label: PF's missing MCP callout and nonstandard crew communication meant the FLCH SPD and A/T HOLD mode changes went unannounced and unnoticed
chain.trigger: the PF did not call out 'flight level change' when he selected FLCH SPD...the PM did not notice that FLCH SPD was engaged

caused_by.evidence: this lack of adherence is likely the reason that the PF did not call out 'flight level change' when he selected FLCH SPD

chain.label: Flight crew's insufficient monitoring let airspeed decay well below target speed unnoticed between 500 and 200 ft
chain.trigger: the flight crew's insufficient monitoring of airspeed indications during the approach resulted from expectancy, increased workload, fatigue, and automation reliance

caused_by.evidence: the thrust levers were still at idle...well above the descent rate...needed to maintain the desired glidepath
flight crew was experiencing fatigue, which likely degraded their performance
reduced the PM's awareness of the PF's actions around the time of the unintended deactivation of automatic airspeed control

chain.label: Airspeed decayed to stick-shaker activation as thrust remained near idle
chain.trigger: the CVR recorded the stick shaker activating, and the lowest airspeed during the approach of about 103 knots was recorded

caused_by.evidence: insufficient flight crew monitoring of airspeed indications during the approach

chain.label: Flight crew delayed initiating a go-around until below 100 ft, after the airplane no longer had performance capability to recover
chain.trigger: the flight crew's delayed execution of a go-around after they became aware that the airplane was below acceptable glidepath and airspeed tolerances

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew did not initiate a go-around until the airplane was below 100 ft, at which point the airplane did not have the performance capability to accomplish a go-around

chain.label: Airplane's main landing gear and aft fuselage struck the seawall short of the runway
chain.trigger: the main landing gear and the aft fuselage struck the seawall, the tail of the airplane broke off at the aft pressure bulkhead

caused_by.evidence: the airplane did not have the performance capability to accomplish a go-around

chain.label: Three passengers fatally injured and dozens seriously injured, including occupants ejected through the ruptured tail
chain.trigger: Three of the 291 passengers were fatally injured; 40 passengers, 8 of the 12 flight attendants, and 1 of the 4 flight crewmembers received serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: impact forces, which exceeded certification limits, resulted in the inflation of two slide/rafts...Six occupants were ejected from the airplane during the impact sequence
